minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to back the North Cemetery expansion design and a separate cemetery road repair request.
minutes.summary: The DPW director briefed the commission on spring cleanup, a compact backhoe, North Cemetery expansion design and cemetery road repairs. The commission discussed remaining plot counts in the North and South cemeteries, and why the Rainmaker software count differs from what is actually available. It voted twice to move forward on the expansion design and the road repair request. A resident objected during public comment, and the exchange ended heatedly before adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Raised handling of federal records such as DD214s, the lot sales fund balance versus the capital and special project requests, a view that the North Cemetery expansion needs stormwater and conservation planning first, and exhumation permits and disclosure when moving a burial.

votes.motion: Approve prior meeting minutes (the motion as heard names January 9th, 2025, though the item was announced as the February 27th meeting).
Go forward with the North Cemetery back lot expansion design, the fifty thousand dollar capital plan request.
Go forward with the special projects warrant article for cemetery road repairs.

budget_items.topic: Compact backhoe in FY26 capital plan
budget_items.what_was_said: A compact backhoe is requested mainly for cemetery grave digging, replacing a shared machine with highway.
The capital plan includes money for expansion design and a contract, which the DPW director believes covers the design.
A tentative special projects article would fund crack sealing and cut-and-patch on cemetery roads.
The DPW director estimated a fireproof cabinet for records could cost up to a stated amount; the commission asked for the cost to be found.

budget_items.topic: Earmark for gravestone restoration, walls and turf
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reviewed a state earmark request covering monument restoration, stone walls and turf, with wall quotes varying widely.
A possible wall in the open hedge area was estimated in a high range and would need a future capital plan.
A member noted plot cost used to be lower and is now higher, and asked how it is split.
A resident said the lot sales fund holds a balance he argued should fund work rather than taxpayers, and cited interest earned.

decisions.decision: The DPW director is to estimate the cost of having someone survey and mark available plots, to be brought back to the commission.
Plot availability data and screenshots will be sent to the group and filed with the minutes; a slide deck of projects, warrant articles and plot data was suggested.
The commission will look into the cost of a fireproof locking cabinet for records, to be discussed later.
Next meeting set for April 24th; a member will meet with Bill beforehand.
The chair will ask the town manager about grant options for the hedge area.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission voted by voice, all in favor, to go forward with the North Cemetery back lot expansion design as a capital plan request.
The commission voted by voice, all in favor, to go forward with a special projects warrant article for cemetery road repairs.
The DPW director is to estimate the cost of having someone survey and mark available plots, and bring it back to the commission.
The commission discussed why the Rainmaker software plot count differs from the plots actually available in the North and South cemeteries.
A resident said during public comment that the lot sales fund balance should pay for work instead of taxpayers; the exchange ended heatedly.

why_it_matters: The expansion design and road repairs are headed toward capital plan and warrant article requests, so they may reach town meeting as spending a resident is asked to vote on.

The lot sales fund balance and the plot-count discrepancy bear on how much cemetery capacity is left and whether the work is paid from that fund or from taxes; the minutes show the question raised but not settled.
